operation_details.item: The user always chooses only free public data sources for market research and avoids paid databases.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the market research work going for the budget review?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Going well. I’m pulling together the competitor and market data now.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Are you using one of the subscription databases, or keeping the research lightweight?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I always stick to free public sources. Government datasets, company filings, industry reports, and other open web sources are usually enough.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That can work well, especially if you document the source dates and reconcile conflicting figures.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I’d rather build a transparent dataset from public information than pay for a database we may only use once.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. What’s the next step after you finish collecting the data?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’ll clean it up, compare the main scenarios, and work the findings into the planning model.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For market research subscriptions, I always choose only free public data sources and avoid paid databases even when accuracy and timeliness matter.
